one_liner: Unicode Consortium's Rust rewrite of ICU; a 2023 first-party post says its line and word segmenters beat ICU4C's break iterators by 19-52%.
what_it_does: ICU4X is the Unicode Consortium's Rust internationalization library. Its icu_segmenter crate finds grapheme, word, sentence (UAX #29) and line (UAX #14, with CSS line-break and word-break options) boundaries. You build a segmenter once (new_auto, new_dictionary, new_lstm or new_for_non_complex_scripts) and call segment_str, segment_utf8, segment_latin1 or segment_utf16, which returns an iterator of code-unit offsets; word_type() and is_word_like() stand in for ICU4C's rule status. It is not a drop-in for ICU4C's BreakIterator. C++ callers use Diplomat-generated headers (icu4x::LineSegmenter::create_auto(), segment(std::string_view) returning a std::unique_ptr iterator whose int32_t next() returns -1 at the end).
how_it_is_fast: Each code point's break property comes from one CodePointTrie lookup. Data generation compiles the segmentation rules into a pairwise break-state table (left property x right property), with intermediate states for rules that need lookahead, and the iterator walks it forward over native UTF-8, Latin-1 or UTF-16 with no UText layer. Data is baked into the binary as zero-copy zerovec structures, and locale tailoring is applied at runtime as a property-table override; per search snippets, the blog credits runtime tailoring for having fewer rule tables. Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese use either an LSTM model (the blog snippet says SIMD made inference about 3x faster than a naive version) or a Char16Trie dictionary, a port of ICU's UCharsTrie. Chinese and Japanese word breaking takes the longest dictionary match and ignores the dictionary's cost values. ICU4C's CjkBreakEngine instead runs an NFKC normalization check and a dynamic-programming minimum-cost search, so it does more work per character.
when_to_use: Rust, WebAssembly, Dart or JS code that needs UAX #29 word, grapheme or sentence boundaries, or UAX #14 line breaking, without linking ICU4C and its separate data file. Compiled data is baked in, and the crate builds as no_std plus alloc.
Text layout or browser-style line breaking that needs CSS options: LineBreakStrictness (strict, normal, loose, anywhere) and LineBreakWordOption (break-all, keep-all).
Size-constrained builds with Thai, Lao, Khmer or Burmese text. The LSTM models replace per-language word dictionaries, and new_auto picks them.
Input that is already UTF-8 or Latin-1. segment_str, segment_utf8 (which tolerates ill-formed input) and segment_latin1 run on those buffers directly, with no UTF-16 conversion and no UText wrapper.
Projects that already use ICU4X for formatting, collation or normalization and want one Unicode-maintained stack.
when_not_to_use: When you need a current, measured win over ICU4C. The only ICU4C comparison is the 2023 first-party post about ICU4X 1.2. Correctness fixes have since changed the segmenter code: LB25/LB8a line rules (PR #4389, Dec 2023), Unicode 15.0 sentence rules, dictionary rewinding and word colon tailoring (both 2.3). Benchmark on your own text.

Chinese or Japanese word segmentation where split quality matters, such as search indexing. Greedy longest match can split ambiguous text differently from ICU4C's cost-minimizing search, and the BudouX/phrase alternative is still an open issue (#1803).

High-throughput Thai, Lao, Khmer or Burmese segmentation through new_auto. It loads the LSTM model, which the docs call more expensive at runtime than the dictionary; use new_dictionary when speed matters more than data size. Issue #7218 (open) reports double line-break opportunities around spaces in Khmer.

C++ projects that cannot add a Rust/cargo build step. You must build the icu_capi library, every segment() call heap-allocates an iterator, and each boundary costs one FFI call that returns int32_t, so offsets past 2^31-1 come back as -1.

Code that needs ICU4C BreakIterator features such as random access (preceding, following, isBoundary) or custom rule strings at runtime. No such methods appear in the segmenter sources read here: the iterators only move forward, and rules are fixed when the data is generated.

integration.form: crate (icu_segmenter, or the icu umbrella crate); static or shared library icu_capi with Diplomat C and C++ headers for other languages
integration.dependencies: icu_collections, icu_provider, zerovec, utf8_iter, smallvec, potential_utf; the default compiled_data feature adds icu_segmenter_data and icu_locale_fallback; the lstm feature adds core_maths
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88 (workspace rust-version for 2.3.x). The C++ headers use std::string_view and std::u16string_view, so C++17 or later (inferred; not stated in the files read).
integration.platforms: any Rust target, including wasm32 and no_std plus alloc; FFI for C, C++, JS (npm), Dart (pub.dev)
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the files read. Segmenter objects are immutable after construction, and each segment_* call returns its own iterator.

gotchas: Choose the constructor deliberately. new_auto means LSTM for Southeast Asian scripts (plus the dictionary for Chinese and Japanese in the word segmenter). new_for_non_complex_scripts treats a Thai run as a single segment and, in the word segmenter, leaves Chinese and Japanese unsegmented. The line segmenter never loads a Chinese/Japanese dictionary, because UAX #14 rules handle CJK.

Rule versions are pinned to the crate's data: the line segmenter defaults to UAX #14 for Unicode 15.1, with separate *_17_* constructors for 17.0. Boundaries can differ from the ICU4C version you compare against.

The experimental _neo_ (V2 state-machine) constructors sit behind the unstable feature. Issue #8522 (Sept 2026, fixed by PR #8523) showed the V2 dictionary path dropping the final breakpoint, so keep them out of production.

The upstream V1 iterator looks up the trie property twice per code point. The unmerged DioxusLabs/icu4x fork PRs #1 and #2 (Sept 2026) report 2.0-2.5x on ASCII prose without LTO but only about 1.1x with LTO, so turn on LTO before judging its speed.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ICU4X when you need line breaking with CSS options plus dictionary- or LSTM-based word segmentation for Southeast Asian and CJK scripts, maintained by the Unicode Consortium. For C++ word and grapheme iteration, uni-algo is header-only and measured 4.8x faster than ICU word breaking (11379.4 vs 2355.47 ms, derived from page data). For grapheme counting in Rust, fast-grapheme-segmenter benchmarks ICU4X's own grapheme segmenter as its slow baseline (1.82 us vs 0.05 us on English).
verified_claims_summary: The only number is from the Unicode blog's ICU4X 1.2 announcement (2023-04-17), known here only through search snippets: line and word segmentation 19.1% and 52.2% faster than ICU4C on non-complex scripts, and 46.9% and 32.1% faster on Chinese. It gives no hardware, compiler, ICU4C version, test text or method, and the repo has no ICU4C harness. Reading the code shows the Chinese word figure does not compare equal work. ICU4X 1.2's dictionary.rs already took the greedy longest match and ignored trie values, while ICU4C's CjkBreakEngine (dictbe.cpp) checks NFKC and runs a minimum-cost dynamic program. The 1.2 segmenter also predates later conformance fixes to line, sentence and word rules.
status_note: Actively developed by the Unicode Consortium's ICU4X technical committee (2.3.x releases; 1.9k stars; 654 open issues). The Unicode-3.0 license is MIT-style and also covers the data, so it is copyable, but C++ use means shipping a Rust-built library.
sources_read: WebSearch: ICU4X segmenter performance compared ICU4C benchmark line word break (snippet of blog.unicode.org/2023/04, page not opened)
